candidate.blueprint_topic: Home oxygen safety and prevention of fire-related harm
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients using supplemental oxygen that oxygen is an oxidizer that can intensify fire and that oxygen equipment must be kept away from clothing and other combustible materials, with valves and fittings free from grease and oil.

options.A: I will keep the oxygen equipment away from clothing and other combustible materials because oxygen can cause or intensify fire
options.B: Oxygen suppresses combustion, so combustible materials may be stored next to the cylinder
options.C: Grease or oil can be applied to oxygen valves and fittings if they become difficult to turn
options.D: Fire precautions are unnecessary as long as the oxygen cylinder itself is not leaking

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The current DailyMed prescription label for compressed oxygen identifies oxygen as an oxidizer that may cause or intensify fire and instructs users to keep and store it away from clothing and other combustible materials. The label also directs users to keep valves and fittings free from grease and oil. B, C, and D contradict these explicit safety warnings. The source item's broader wording about smoking, open flames, and all flammable materials was narrowed to the exact precautions directly supported by the verified current label.
candidate.source_claim_supported: The current official oxygen label directly supports the fire-hazard teaching that oxygen is an oxidizer that may intensify fire, should be kept away from combustible materials, and requires oil- and grease-free valves and fittings.
